sets.name: Uroda
sets.dek: Six groups of one surname — three at Karlobag, one dead man of Šibenik, and a soldier's family at Drniš and another at Betina. Only the top lane is ours, and the joins between the others are drawn dotted because no document makes them.

lanes.label: Šibenik (Dolac) — the name from 1687 to 1767; four households by 1692; Franciscus with Anna, a master by 1725; Georgius (b. 6 Oct 1694, son of Dominicus and Lucietta; d. 1754) and his son Dominicus, an elder Dominicus (dead by 1746), Antonius (m. Godfather («Mr / Dñ Francus Vroda», nearly always beside an Angela Julioli) at Dolac baptisms on 19 Mar 1725, 6 Jul and 26 Oct 1728, 7 Jan, 23 Aug and 12 Sep 1729 and 12 Feb 1730, and again 25 Apr 1733, 30 Jan 1735 and, as «Magister», 12 Oct 1738. Dead by 6 May 1742, when his daughter Antonia, wife of a Joannes Biliznich, is called «filia q. Francisci Vrodda de hac Parochia S. Marci» — and dead on 15 Nov 1738 («Magister Franciscus Vroda», buried at the Holy Trinity)
Georgius Uroda (Magister; born 6 Oct 1694, died 17 Aug 1754)

**Baptised in the cathedral on 10 Oct 1694, «ex Coniugibus Dominico et Lucietta Vroda»** — the age at death, «60», fits to the month. Godfather «Georgius Urodich» at Dolac 28 Jan 1720 and 27 Dec 1721 (perhaps already 28 Oct 1715); a master, already married, in 1738 («uxor Mri Georgij Vroda»; his wife is not named Maria); ALIVE on 4 Aug 1746, when «Dominico Vrodda, filio Magistri Georgii» is a witness; and DEAD by 13 Feb 1757, when his son Dominicus is called «filius qd. Georgij Vroda»; very probably the «Dominus Georgius Vroda aetatis annorum 60» who died on 17 Aug 1754 and was buried at S. Dominic; a daughter Magdalena, «filia Magistri Georgii Vrode», was buried 29 Oct 1740
Magister Dominicus Uroda (son of the late Georgius)

A «Mr. Domcus [Dominicus?] Vroda» is godfather at Dolac on 27 Jan 1726; godfather («Magister Dominicus Vroda») 1 Jan and 23 Apr 1741; father, with a wife FLORIA, of Lucia (born 12 Dec 1744) and Vittoria (born 10 May 1745); godfather 27 Jun 1749, 20 Mar 1752 and 6 Jul 1755; on 4 Aug 1746 a witness «Dominicus Vrodda, filius Magistri Georgii»; on 13 Feb 1757 «Dominicus filius qd. Georgij Vroda»; on 11 Sep 1757 «Dominicus Vroda Pictor» (a painter); witness at Dolac marriages 11 Jan 1756, 11 Sep 1759 and 10 Aug 1762 and at the cathedral 3 Jun 1767. Two masters of the name seem to be mixed here: a Lucia «ux. q. Mag. Dominici Vrodda», aged about 77, dies on 21 Jun 1746, so an ELDER Magister Dominicus was dead by then; the younger, son of Georgius, has an infant son Paulus buried 7 Jan 1744 — and at the cathedral: Joseph Joannes (born 16 Dec 1739, ceremonies 7 Jun 1740) and Anna (born May 1741; 6 Aug 1741), «filius/filia Magistri Dominici et Florae Vroda», in no Dolac book
«testibus Joseph Fevetti, et Joanne filio Dominici Uroda» — a son of a Dominicus Uroda, of an age to witness
Antonia Vrodda, wife of Joannes Mestrovich alias Calafat
Mother of Franceschina, baptised at Dolac 23 October 1746 — an Uroda daughter, her father not named

«Georgius filius Joannis [Presrou?] de Flumine, alias Biliznich, et Antoniae filiae q. Francisci Vrodda de hac Parochia S. Marci» — Antonia, a daughter of the late Franciscus Uroda, and her son Georgius BILIZNICH (not Uroda), born 17 April 1742
ends: **At Šibenik the father is now found: Georgius (b. 6 Oct 1694, d. 17 Aug 1754) was the son of the Magister Dominicus and Lucietta Vroda of the Dolac parish, baptised at the cathedral.** That Georgius died in 1754; Georgius Uroda of Karlobag (ahnentafel 108) was alive from 1763 to 1791, so he is not the Šibenik Georgius — he named his first son Dominicus in 1764, as the Šibenik Georgius did, which keeps the name pattern but proves nothing. Georgius Uroda of Karlobag (ahnentafel 108) named his first son Dominicus in 1764. At Šibenik a Dominicus Uroda, a master, is «filius Magistri Georgii» (4 Aug 1746) and «filius qd. Georgij Vroda» (13 Feb 1757) — a Magister Georgius, alive in 1746 and dead by 1757, and a Dominicus. If Georgius of Karlobag is a son of that Dominicus he is named for his grandfather and his first son for his father; that is a pattern in the names, not a document, and none of the three Dolac baptism books (1685–1762) holds a baptism of him. There was also a Magister Georgius Uroda at Šibenik, married, in 1738: the Georgius of Karlobag cannot be that man if he first fathered a child in 1764, but he could be a grandson or a namesake. The Šibenik Georgius died on 17 August 1754 (aged about 60), so he is not the Karlobag Georgius, who is alive from 1763 to 1791; and the Šibenik Georgius's son Dominicus has only daughters and an infant Paulus in the Dolac books, no Georgius

The dead Dume of Šibenik (d. before 1739) is the one Šibenik Uroda with a recorded child (the bride Simona of 1739); Franciscus, Georgius and Dominicus, masters of the same years, are candidates for his sons, but no register read says so — and the one father named at Šibenik is «Georgius» (1757), not Dume

sets.note: One spelling is not a search. The registers write Uroda, urode, vrode, Urodan, Urada; the index reads one Karlobag father as Sime, spells Dume's children Urode (so a search for Uroda misses them), and reads one Drniš father four ways (Janpao, Ganpas, Pompio, Tomaso) where the pages say Pampao and Pompeo. At Karlobag in 1734 a priest writes «Dume urode alliti Kovaca» — a by-name, a smith's — and before the 1730s the book has no Uroda at all, so a baptism of the man himself would sit under another surname. See The Second Name.
sets.owes: For Uroda that is: Dume's baptism (likely under the by-name Kovač, in the 1700s), the marriage of Georgius and Maria (not in Karlobag's marriage book 1736–1804, not in the index under any «Urod*» spelling, not in the Šibenik cathedral marriage book 1752–1770 nor the Dolac parish marriage book 1752–1764, both read entry by entry; perhaps Varoš before 1764, whose book begins only that year, or a place not filmed), Maria's maiden name (Barach, of Šibenik, is the best candidate — her first child's godfather), and the Šibenik baptisms themselves: all three Dolac baptism books (1685–1700, 1701–1731 and 1731–1762) are now read through — no baptism of a Georgius, Dominicus or Dume Uroda, but a Dominicus «son of Magister Georgius» (1746, the Dolac marriage book) and «son of the late Georgius» (1757); the Dolac marriage book 1701–1764 is read to its end (no marriage of Georgius, Dominicus or Dume); the Dolac deaths book is read for September 1738 – March 1756 (Franciscus died 15 Nov 1738) (Georgius died 17 August 1754; a Magister Antonius with daughters buried 1742; a Lucia, widow of a Magister Dominicus, 1746) but not for 1738–1740, 1754–1757 or before 1738; the cathedral births are read only as a margin scan for 1693–1702 (which found Georgius's own baptism, 6 Oct 1694, and his brother Simeon) and 1737–1744 (which found two more children of Dominicus and Flora); still to read are the cathedral births 1702–1737 and after 1740 and before 1693, and the Varoš births (1711–1767), where the baptism of a Georgius or a Dominicus, or of a «Georgius filius Dominici», would say whose son Georgius of Karlobag is (the Betina and Drniš ones have been opened and are other families).

sets.name: Smojver
sets.dek: At Karlobag the name is written in two ways, with and without the by-name «Vukić», and a second large body of the exact spelling sits at Cesarica. Only the Vukić line is ours; the others are drawn apart until a register joins them.

Forty-odd index lines in later decades, all after 1845: households that moved, probably out of the Karlobag–Cesarica stock, but not shown to
sets.note: Why two lanes at Karlobag. The tree's Smojver are called Vukić in the marriage of 1774 and the baptism of 1781 («Smojver Vukich»), and the 1776 death says «called Vukcich». The Paulus Smojver who baptises in 1763 is written without it. A by-name marks which house of a surname is meant (see The Second Name), so the two are kept apart until something says Paulus is a Vukić too.
sets.owes: For Smojver that is: Josiph's baptism of 1731, whether Paulus is a Vukić, and whether the Cesarica Smojver came from Karlobag or the other way (the Cesarica index lines begin in 1810 and the Karlobag ones in 1768, which may only mean that Cesarica's books are indexed from 1810).

sets.name: Pilipić
sets.dek: The name is written Pilepich, Pilipich and Pilipić, and the index has it by the thousand in the Rijeka–Kastav area and at «Vitipolis». Only the Karlobag line of Jacobus, captain of the port, is ours.

sets.note: Why only one lane. The index has well over a thousand lines of the name, but every cluster outside Karlobag is a body of index lines, not a family anyone has followed. They are listed below the figure as not yet on any lane rather than drawn as families: a lane is a household the registers show, and these have not been shown.
sets.owes: For Pilipić that is: the captain's baptism (not at Karlobag: the index has no Pilipić baptism there before 1739, and 1700–1730 holds none under any spelling — so probably at Kastav or Rijeka, where two Jacobus Pilepich of 1705 and 1708 are the candidates), whether the Jakov of 1739 is he, and a second family of the name at Karlobag before anyone is called a stranger to it.

sets.name: Bacchi
sets.dek: A rare name, and the one with the best lead on this site: a Caietanus Bachi baptised at Pag in 1728, the son of a patrician, who may be the Caetanus who married at Karlobag in 1753.

sets.note: What the 1728 page does and does not say. It names a child Caietanus Antonius ac Gregorius, born 12 March 1728, to Dno Angelo Bachi, Patricio and Dna Oliva, at Pag. On the Karlobag side everything is circumstance — the rare name, the age, a daughter called Oliva like the Pag mother. And the tree's Angelo (ahnentafel 428) is not evidence: he and his Catharina come only from a different baptism, of 12 January 1779, of a Caetanus Antonius at Karlobag whose godmother is Maria Uroda — a second Bachi household in the town, which the tree has wrongly welded onto the elder Caetanus. So the Pag baptism is a candidate, strong and unproved, and the 1779 household a separate lane.
sets.owes: For Bacchi that is: a Karlobag entry that names Caetanus's father or his town (the marriage of 1753 does not), his death before October 1760 (Karlobag's death book begins in 1774, so that is not filmed), and the Pag baptisms of his siblings read from the pages, not the index.
